purpose: Evaluate model and threshold feasibility under progressively stricter minimum recall requirements.

selection_rule.feasibility: A model-threshold combination is feasible when recall is greater than or equal to the specified minimum recall requirement.
selection_rule.primary_selection_criterion: Highest F1 among feasible thresholds for each model and recall scenario.

analysis.evaluation_method: Pooled out-of-fold predictions from the development set.
analysis.purpose: Determine which models and thresholds can satisfy progressively stricter failure-detection requirements.

key_findings.60_percent: All three models had at least one feasible tested threshold.
key_findings.70_percent: Logistic Regression and Random Forest had feasible thresholds; Decision Tree did not.
key_findings.80_percent: Only Random Forest had a feasible tested threshold.
key_findings.90_percent: Only Random Forest had a feasible tested threshold.
key_findings.95_percent: No tested model-threshold combination reached the minimum recall requirement.

observations: Increasing the minimum recall requirement progressively reduced the number of feasible model-threshold combinations.
Random Forest remained feasible under the strictest recall requirements that were achievable in the tested threshold grid.
At a 90 percent minimum recall requirement, Random Forest required a threshold of 0.05 and produced substantially more false positives.
No evaluated model-threshold combination reached 95 percent recall.
research_decision: Use minimum recall as an explicit constraint in subsequent cost-sensitive and final model-selection analysis.
